rows.source: HSE motor-vehicle isocyanate paint-spraying safety
rows.verified: Two-pack motor-vehicle paints and many lacquers can contain isocyanates; a water-based label does not mean a product is isocyanate-free.

rows.source: HSE motor-vehicle isocyanate paint-spraying safety
rows.verified: Isocyanates used in vehicle spray painting are a leading cause of occupational asthma and can also cause dermatitis.

rows.source: HSE motor-vehicle isocyanate paint-spraying safety
rows.verified: Spray painting produces a large amount of fine, often invisible airborne mist that can be inhaled.

rows.source: HSE motor-vehicle isocyanate paint-spraying safety
rows.verified: Isocyanate spraying should normally be carried out in an enclosed extracted spray booth or spray room.

rows.source: HSE motor-vehicle isocyanate paint-spraying safety
rows.verified: Air-fed breathing apparatus should be worn while isocyanate mist is present, including during the booth clearance period.

rows.source: HSE motor-vehicle isocyanate paint-spraying safety
rows.verified: The spray-booth or room clearance time should be measured, displayed and understood by workers before visors are lifted or the area is entered unprotected.

rows.source: HSE motor-vehicle isocyanate paint-spraying safety
rows.verified: Biological monitoring using urine samples can check whether respiratory protection and working practices are controlling isocyanate exposure.

rows.source: HSE motor-vehicle isocyanate paint-spraying safety
rows.verified: Employers must provide suitable information, instruction and training, and isocyanate-use training should be reviewed and repeated when required.

rows.source: HSE motor-vehicle isocyanate paint-spraying safety
rows.verified: Vehicle-paint exposure risk depends on paint chemistry, spraying method, booth extraction, clearance time, RPE condition, work practices and worker susceptibility.

rows.source: HSE motor-vehicle isocyanate paint-spraying safety
rows.verified: HSE motor-vehicle-paint evidence is process-, product-, booth-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level asthma probability.

rows.source: HSE tyre removal and inflation safety
rows.verified: Tyre removal, replacement and inflation should be undertaken only by competent staff.

rows.source: HSE tyre removal and inflation safety
rows.verified: Tyre work hazards include manual-handling injuries, hand-tool injuries and compressed-air accidents.

rows.source: HSE tyre removal and inflation safety
rows.verified: Inflated tyres contain substantial stored energy that increases with pressure and tyre surface area.

rows.source: HSE tyre removal and inflation safety
rows.verified: A tyre rupture can release explosive force through a broad trajectory, so operators must remain outside the likely blast path.

rows.source: HSE tyre removal and inflation safety
rows.verified: A clip-on chuck and sufficiently long airline allow the operator to stand clear while controlling inflation.

rows.source: HSE tyre removal and inflation safety
rows.verified: Higher-pressure commercial tyres may require enhanced controls, including a suitable restraint during inflation above the stated seating pressure.

rows.source: HSE tyre removal and inflation safety
rows.verified: Multi-piece wheel and tyre assemblies should be checked at low initial pressure before higher pressure is applied.

rows.source: HSE tyre removal and inflation safety
rows.verified: Tyre cages or other restraining devices are required for hazardous wheel types such as split-rim assemblies, alongside safe maintenance isolation.

rows.source: HSE tyre removal and inflation safety
rows.verified: Tyre-inflation risk depends on tyre size, pressure, damage, wheel design, seating, restraint, operator position and competence.

rows.source: HSE tyre removal and inflation safety
rows.verified: HSE tyre evidence is wheel-, tyre-, pressure-, task-, operator- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level explosion probability.
